question.answer: interactions.review with params conversationId and requestRef, body.answer (body.data accepted); a single_string form takes the text, a multi-field form takes one JSON object, and the answer is validated against requested_schema before it is sent; a successful answer is the state transition, because the answered question leaves the window and no further frame is published for it
question.answerable: only the newest question of the open conversation is answered; any other reference answers 409 NOT_PENDING and never reaches the agent, and a question whose schema this host cannot read answers 501 QUESTION_UNSUPPORTED

raw_events.content: one bounded, control-stripped line '[event type] title status raw' for every event the chat has no row of its own for

stream_events.usage: one agent usage report becomes one message.stream row of type acp_context_usage with content {used, size, cost?}; a report this build cannot read keeps its bounded raw line, and usage.read answers the same numbers as its own route
stream_events.complete: the turn boundary becomes one message.stream row of type finish with content {conversation_id, turn_id, status: finished, stop_reason, outcome}, and the same boundary is announced once as the named turn.completed event whether or not this host accepted the turn itself
stream_events.session_info: one agent session fact (a retitled session and the like) becomes one message.stream row of type tips with content.type info, carrying the bounded raw line plus title, status and session_id
stream_events.resolved: a resolved interaction stays silent: the product's own bookkeeping row covers something the chat already drew while it was pending, and an approval that left the window is withdrawn through confirmation.remove
stream_events.unknown: every other event still becomes the bounded tips/info raw line, so nothing the agent sent vanishes

link_events: the open conversation's host link is published on the same event channel from the product's own reconnect bookkeeping, without a poll of its own: realtime.reconnected once the link is usable again (the name the renderer reconciles history and approvals on), realtime.disconnected while it is lost or waiting for the user, both with {conversation_id, host_id, state (connected, offline or needs_user), link_state, reconnected, needs_user}; a frame is published only when the kind of that state changes, and conversations.list reports the same fact per row as offline and link_state
local_network_permission: the renderer host asks for the nearby-devices grant from API 36 on and for local-network access from API 37 on, once, the first time an action has to reach a host over the LAN (detection.refresh, hosts.refresh, conversations.create, project.read, search.sessions); until that grant is there those routes answer 403 LOCAL_NETWORK_PERMISSION_REQUIRED with the reason and the host shows the degraded access on its own surface, so a refusal is never silent and the action can be retried after granting

challenges.read: GET /api/challenges -> data.challenge {id, host_id, host_name, kind, message, secret}, or null while no connection asks for input; kind is host_key, password or key_passphrase, host_id is null once that host is gone, and no credential is ever part of this payload
challenges.answer: POST /api/challenges/:challengeId/answer with body.answer; a host_key challenge continues on 'accept' and cancels on anything else, an omitted or empty answer cancels the request, and the answer is never stored, logged or echoed back; 409 CHALLENGE_NOT_PENDING for an id that is no longer the pending one

messages_before: GET /api/conversations/:conversationId/messages/before?before=<cursor>&limit=n loads one older page from the history store and answers it in the messages.list page shape, with has_more_after true because the caller still holds the newer part; 409 HISTORY_EXHAUSTED when the product holds no older page, 500 HISTORY_LOAD_FAILED when it cannot be read, 422 INVALID_CURSOR when the cursor is not in the loaded window
conversations_create: POST /api/conversations with params hostId and body.agent plus body.cwd (agent and cwd are accepted as params too); data is the created conversation row plus session_id (the Agent's own native id), agent, cwd and created=true; 404 HOST_NOT_FOUND, 422 AGENT_UNKNOWN or INVALID_CWD, 409 SESSION_CREATE_FAILED carrying the repository's own reason (a directory the host cannot use fails as itself), 409 SESSION_ID_UNKNOWN when the Agent returned no native id
terminal_open: POST /api/conversations/:conversationId/terminal or POST /api/hosts/:hostId/terminal -> data {host_id, host_name, agent, cwd, target, command}, plus conversation_id and session_id on the conversation path, the command being the product's own terminal route command for this host's Agent target, built by ShellCommands.start and wrapped once for that target; neither route is a GET because the caller names a directory in the request body, and neither launches anything; the target is one conversation — whose Agent, session id and working directory the host reads from its own index, so it does not have to be open — or one saved host, which has none of its own: its Agent is the Agent of the conversation this product holds for that host while there is one, otherwise the first Agent that host's probe found installed, and its directory is body.cwd, which replaces the conversation's own directory when the conversation path sends one; 422 INVALID_CWD without a usable body.cwd for a host target or for a non-string one, 422 TERMINAL_TARGET_UNKNOWN naming neither target, 409 WORKSPACE_UNKNOWN without a usable directory for a conversation, 409 AGENT_UNAVAILABLE for a host holding no Agent any probe found, 404 HOST_NOT_FOUND or CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND for an unknown target, 501 TERMINAL_UNSUPPORTED for a target this app has no shell entry for; no credential is ever part of this payload
terminal_command: POST /api/conversations/:conversationId/terminal/command or POST /api/hosts/:hostId/terminal/command -> the same answer as terminal_open, with the same body, the same directory rules and the same refusals: on this host one terminal route runs the Agent's own TUI, so the command is the ShellCommands.start command of that conversation or that host's Agent; the route is named separately so the caller can hand it to the terminal as the Agent's TUI rather than as a plain shell, and nothing is launched here either
hosts_refresh: POST /api/hosts/:hostId/refresh probes that host through the repository's refresh entry and rescans its session index; data {host_id, refreshed, sessions, detection}; 500 HOST_REFRESH_FAILED keeps the code and reason the repository reported
hosts_list: GET /api/hosts lists the product's own SSH hosts; every row carries id (`host-<id>`), nickname, hostname, port, username, protocol, os_type, agent_target, target, target_supported, session_count (how many conversations the session index holds for that host, a real 0 when that index was never read) and detection {checked, agents[{id, state, executable, version, capabilities, error}]}, the capabilities being exactly what that host's probe declared and null until one answered. hosts.create and hosts.update answer the same row
conversations_list: GET /api/conversations lists one row per indexed (host, agent, session); every row carries offline (true while the product holds a link state for that host that is not connected), link_state (connected, disconnected, retrying, needs_user or unknown when the product never observed that host), cached (true while the row comes from the index cache rather than a read of that host in this pass) and workspace {host_id, cwd} for grouping, beside the existing id, name, project_id, status, runtime and extra fields
search_sessions: GET /api/search?q=<query>&host_id=<hostId>&agent=<kind>&limit=<n> searches across conversations in the two ways this host can honestly search: the index's own title, preview and directory fields, and the content of the selected remote transcripts (one bounded, read-only scan per host). data {query, items, total, has_more, coverage}; one item is kind=index with conversation_id, host_id, agent, session_id, cwd, field (title, preview or cwd), snippet, source (remote or cached) or kind=content with the same identity fields plus snippet, file, line, anchor (file#line) and clipped, both carrying openable (false when that conversation is no longer held and cannot be opened from here); coverage {complete, truncated, failed_sources[{host_id, code: source_unreadable, reason}], problems[stable codes such as search_timeout or search_tool_missing], skipped[{conversation_id, host_id, agent, session_id, code}], roots, searched_sessions, index_complete, remote_rows, cached_rows} is false while any part of the range stayed unread, so a caller never renders it as a history without that text; 422 INVALID_QUERY for an empty, control-carrying or over-long query or an out-of-range limit, 404 HOST_NOT_FOUND and 422 AGENT_UNKNOWN for filters nothing could match, 500 SEARCH_FAILED when the search itself could not run; nothing is opened, sent or written by a search
inbox_list: GET /api/inbox is the read-only attention projection over the open conversation alone - the only one whose approvals, questions, failure and running turn this host holds - answered as data {items[{conversation_id, host_id, agent, session_id, reasons, pending_approvals, pending_questions, last_error, summary, updated_at}], total, read_only: true, scope: open_conversation}; a conversation reporting nothing has no row, an unreported time stays null, and this route approves, answers or changes nothing
queue_list: GET /api/queue answers every message still waiting for its conversation, oldest first, as data {items[{queue_id, host_id, agent, session_id, conversation_id, kind (notify or request), text, created_at, state, pending}], total, stats{stored, pending, delivered, dropped}}; reading the queue sends and delivers nothing
queue_send: POST /api/queue with body.conversation_id, or body.host_id plus body.agent and body.session_id, plus body.kind (notify or request) and body.text queues one message for another conversation; the target must be a conversation the product already holds, the text must be non-empty and within the message bound; data {queue_id, conversation_id, host_id, agent, session_id, kind, state: pending, queued: true, delivered: false} claims only what is queued, because a request is delivered by opening that conversation and never here; 404 CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND for a target the product does not hold, 422 INVALID_KIND, 422 INVALID_CONTENT, 422 QUEUE_REFUSED when the queue itself refused the row, 500 QUEUE_UNAVAILABLE when it cannot be read or written
queue_cancel: DELETE /api/queue/:queueId withdraws one queued message so it can never be delivered later; data {cancelled: true, queue_id, delivered: false} never claims a delivery, and the product's queue records a withdrawn message as taken by its conversation because that is the only terminal state it keeps; 422 INVALID_QUEUE_ID for a malformed id, 404 QUEUE_NOT_FOUND for an id the queue does not hold as pending, 409 QUEUE_NOT_PENDING for a message its conversation already took
reference_pack: POST /api/conversations/:conversationId/reference builds one bounded context pack of that conversation's own loaded window through the same AgentSessionReference projection the Compose quote uses, as data {conversation_id, host_id, host, agent, session_id, cwd, status (complete, trimmed or empty), text, quoted_count, omitted_count, cut_count, sent: false}; the text names what the window, the character budget and the item budget left out, and preparing a pack starts no model call; 409 CONVERSATION_NOT_OPEN when that conversation is not the open one or is not ready yet, 404 CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND for a conversation the product does not hold
index_clear: POST /api/index/clear drops the session index cache through the repository's own clear entry and answers data {cleared: true, sessions_before, sessions}, the second count being what the index holds afterwards; the confirmation a user must give is the front end's step, hosts, detections, drafts and the queue are separate stores, and 500 INDEX_CLEAR_FAILED keeps the code and reason the repository reported
